summary.title: The Architecture of Open Source Applications
summary.one_liner: A two-volume collection in which the authors of about four dozen open source applications explain how their programs are structured and why.
keywords: major components of open source programs
how open source projects are designed
architecture of hadoop distributed file system
takeaways: Experienced developers explain the major components of each program, how they interact, and the reasons behind their design.
The book lists 25 chapters covering projects such as Asterisk, LLVM, Mercurial, Eclipse, Hadoop HDFS, Selenium WebDriver and Battle For Wesnoth.
The stated aim is to help developers learn from other programs' successes and mistakes instead of repeating them.
Junior developers are pointed to it to learn how experienced colleagues think; intermediate and senior developers can see how peers solved hard design problems.
The work is licensed under Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 Unported, with royalties from sales donated to Amnesty International.
summary.summary: This is the landing page for a two-volume book collection in which the authors of about four dozen open source applications describe their software's structure, major components, interactions, and lessons learned. The page opens with the motivation that developers rarely study great programs the way architects study buildings, and then provides a table of contents with 25 chapters, each written by a project's contributors. It also includes the license terms and a call for volunteers to report errors, translate content, or write new chapters on other projects.
